newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Goodman aims for 20 pct sales growth in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Goodman aims for 20 pct sales growth in Asia.

text.p: Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Thursday it was aiming to achieve annual sales growth of 20 percent from Asian-related business.

"We see no reason why we can't achieve (sales) growth of 20 percent a year, that's what we are aiming for," Goodman Fielder managing director David Hearn told reporters after a Committee for Economic Development of Australia luncheon address.
Hearn said the company already had export sales from Australia to Asian markets of about A$130 million a year, and sales from existing Asian operations also of A$130 million a year.
Hearn said he believed the marketing of Australian produce in Asia still left a lot to be desired.
"Australia needs to develop a reputation for food like the French have for perfume," he said.
Hearn said Australia had all the basic ingredients to satisfy the Asian market but needed to exploit them in an intelligent and competitive way.

Goodman Fielder was in a position to make acquisitions to complement its Asian growth strategy, Hearn said, and the company believed its gearing was low enough to raise between A$300-A$500 million of debt comfortably.
But Hearn said the company wasn't contemplating any acquisitions of a size where it would need to raise equity in the near future.
He declined to comment to reporters on rival Australian food group Burns, Philp & Co Ltd, in which New Zealand investor Graeme Hart last week purchased a 14.9 percent stake.
Goodman Fielder has been seen by analysts as a potential buyer of Burns Philp's global yeast operations.
Goodman Fielder is Australasia's largest food group, with annual sales of about A$2.5 billion.
